feat(MOS): DWARF CFI emission for MOS frame lowering (#601)

Enable source-level debugging on MOS 6502 by teaching LLVM to emit
DWARF CFI describing the target's dual-stack unwinding, and by giving
static-stack and zero-page locals real debug locations.

Dual-stack CFI:
- Hardware stack (0x0100-0x01FF) holds return addresses (JSR-pushed)
  and hardware-stack callee-saved registers.
- Soft stack (RS0-relative) holds locals and soft-stack callee-saved
  registers.
- Every hardware-stack address is normalized as ((S+offset) & 0xFF) |
  0x0100, so 8-bit and 16-bit S values both work and S may wrap within
  the stack page.
- The CFA is hardware-stack based for the whole function. The soft
  stack is described by its own rules, so no rule depends on which
  stack the CFA is based on.

CIE (the frame at function entry, set up in createMOSMCAsmInfo):
- CFA = normalized(S+3).
- PC = DW_CFA_val_expression that reads the two return-address bytes
  independently (they are non-consecutive when S wraps) and adds 1,
  because JSR pushes return_PC - 1.
- Caller's S = normalized(S+2). This must be explicit: CFA is S+3, so a
  debugger's default of "caller SP = CFA" is one byte high.
- RS0 = same value. DWARF's default for an unmentioned register is
  undefined, which would leave the caller's RS0 unrecoverable at entry.

Hardware stack:
- emitHardwareStackCFI() re-describes CFA, PC and S immediately after
  every PHA in the prologue and every PLA in the epilogue.
- ISRs: the hardware pushes P and the exact return PC (3 bytes). The
  interrupt-entry layout is described from the first instruction,
  ahead of the CLD; P's save slot is described, and the recovered PC
  has no +1.

Soft stack:
- The caller's RS0 is a DW_CFA_val_expression, Base + the prologue's
  adjustment, emitted right after the prologue's decrement. Base is RS0,
  or the frame pointer once it is set (RS0 then moves in the body), and
  RS0 again after the epilogue copies the frame pointer back. RS0
  returns to its CIE rule after the epilogue's increment.
- Soft-stack callee-saved registers are described with
  DW_CFA_expression at Base + their frame offset, the same offset
  eliminateFrameIndex uses (for ISRs, without the extra atomicity page),
  and restored before the epilogue moves RS0.

Layout:
- CFIFixup is enabled, with resetCFIToInitialState(), so blocks laid
  out after an epilogue get the right state (shrink wrapping, multiple
  epilogues).
- The register scavenger's restore is placed after CFI directives that
  directly follow its last use, so they take effect at the instruction
  they describe.

Debug locations for static-stack and zero-page locals:
- A new TargetFrameLowering::replaceFrameIndexDebugOperand() hook, empty
  by default, lets PEI's replaceFrameIndexDebugInstr hand frame-index
  debug operands to the target. MOS rewrites those of static-stack and
  zero-page locals into the static-stack target index (later resolved to
  the per-function static-stack alias) or the zero-page stack symbol.
  The generic path would substitute $noreg + offset and drop
  DW_AT_location. Indirect DBG_VALUEs absorb the indirection as a
  leading DW_OP_deref, so the result is a memory location (DW_OP_addr).
  Frame-index (dbg.declare) variables were already handled by
  MOSAsmPrinter::getFunctionFrameSymbol(). Fixes #621.

Expression-form CFI via MOS-only helpers:

DW_CFA_expression, DW_CFA_val_expression, and DW_CFA_def_cfa_expression
have no first-class constructors in MCCFIInstruction upstream. Rather
than add cross-target mechanism (as originally proposed in
llvm-mos/llvm-mos#568), MOSCFIExprHelpers.h provides MOS-only inline
helpers with first-class-shaped signatures that internally call
MCCFIInstruction::createEscape and hand-assemble the DWARF byte
sequence. If upstream ever grows real constructors, migration is a
body swap on these helpers with no call-site churn.

Known gaps: hardware-stack and static-stack callee-saved registers have
no save-slot rules (TODO), and hardware stack pushes outside the
prologue and epilogue proper have no CFI: the scavenger's A save around
stack adjustments and soft-stack CSR saves, stack-based register
copies, and the P save.

Tests: cfi-cie.ll checks the CIE; cfi-soft-stack.ll ties each soft-stack
rule to the instructions it describes; frame-pointer-cfi.ll checks the
frame pointer rules; dbg-value-static-local.ll checks memory-location
DW_AT_location for static-stack and zero-page locals; the autogenerated
MOS tests are regenerated with update_llc_test_checks.py and
update_mir_test_checks.py.

Verified end to end by debugging a program under MAME's gdbstub with
LLDB: stopped mid-prologue, in the body, mid-epilogue and at the RTS of
a soft-stack function, the unwound caller RS0, S and PC are identical
and equal the values after `finish`; a caller's soft-stack locals read
the same from a callee's epilogue as from the caller itself.

+; RUN: llc -mtriple=mos -filetype=obj < %s -o %t.o
+; RUN: llvm-dwarfdump --debug-frame --eh-frame %t.o | FileCheck %s
+
+; The CIE describes the MOS frame at function entry. LLDB's MOS ABI decodes
+; these same initial instructions from MCAsmInfo for its function-entry unwind
+; plan, so this is the only place the rules are written down.
+;
+;   CFA       = normalized(S + 3)
+;   caller PC = byte(normalized(S + 1)) | byte(normalized(S + 2)) << 8, + 1
+;   caller S  = normalized(S + 2)
+;   RS0       = same value
+; where normalized(x) = (x & 0xff) | 0x100.
+
+target triple = "mos"
+

+  ret void
+}
+
+; CHECK:      CIE
+; CHECK:      Return address column: 5
+; CHECK:      DW_CFA_def_cfa_expression: DW_OP_breg4 S+3, DW_OP_const1u 0xff, DW_OP_and, DW_OP_const2u 0x100, DW_OP_or
+; CHECK-NEXT: DW_CFA_val_expression: PC DW_OP_breg4 S+1, DW_OP_const1u 0xff, DW_OP_and, DW_OP_const2u 0x100, DW_OP_or, DW_OP_deref_size 0x1, DW_OP_breg4 S+2, DW_OP_const1u 0xff, DW_OP_and, DW_OP_const2u 0x100, DW_OP_or, DW_OP_deref_size 0x1, DW_OP_const1u 0x8, DW_OP_shl, DW_OP_or, DW_OP_plus_uconst 0x1
+; CHECK-NEXT: DW_CFA_val_expression: S DW_OP_breg4 S+2, DW_OP_const1u 0xff, DW_OP_and, DW_OP_const2u 0x100, DW_OP_or
+; CHECK-NEXT: DW_CFA_same_value: RS0

+; RUN: llc -mtriple=mos -O2 -enable-tail-merge=0 < %s \
+; RUN:   | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=ASM
+; RUN: llc -mtriple=mos -O2 -enable-tail-merge=0 -filetype=obj < %s -o %t.o
+; RUN: llvm-dwarfdump --eh-frame %t.o | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=CFI \
+; RUN:   --implicit-check-not=DW_CFA_def_cfa: \
+; RUN:   --implicit-check-not=DW_CFA_val_offset
+
+; The CFA is always based on the hardware stack; the soft stack is described
+; by value expressions for the caller's RS0 and by expressions for the save
+; slots of soft-stack callee-saved registers. Each check below ties a CFI rule
+; to the code it describes.
+
+declare void @ext()
+declare void @use(ptr)
+declare i8 @g(i8)
+
+; A soft-stack frame without a frame pointer: the caller's RS0 is RS0 plus the
+; frame size from the instruction after the prologue's decrement until the
+; epilogue's increment, and the CIE's rule afterwards.
+define void @soft_frame(i8 %n) {
+; The prologue subtracts 4 from RS0 (adding 0xfffc); the caller's RS0 is RS0+4
+; from the next instruction on.
+; ASM-LABEL: soft_frame:
+; ASM:         adc #252
+; ASM-NEXT:    sta __rc0
+; ASM-NEXT:    lda __rc1
+; ASM-NEXT:    adc #255
+; ASM-NEXT:    sta __rc1
+; ASM-NEXT:    .cfi_escape 0x16, 0x80, 0x80, 0x0c, 0x05, 0x92, 0x80, 0x80, 0x0c, 0x04
+; The epilogue adds 4 back; RS0 then holds the caller's value.
+; ASM:         adc #4
+; ASM-NEXT:    sta __rc0
+; ASM-NEXT:    lda __rc1
+; ASM-NEXT:    adc #0
+; ASM-NEXT:    sta __rc1
+; ASM-NEXT:    .cfi_restore llvm_mos_rs0
+; ASM-NEXT:    rts
+; CFI:       FDE
+; CFI:         DW_CFA_val_expression: RS0 DW_OP_bregx RS0+4
+; CFI:         DW_CFA_restore_extended: RS0
+  %buf = alloca [4 x i8]
+  call void @use(ptr %buf)
+  %m = add i8 %n, -1
+  call void @soft_frame(i8 %m)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; A frame pointer and a variable-sized object: once the frame pointer is set,
+; RS0 moves in the body, so the caller's RS0 is described relative to RS15.
+define void @fp_frame(i16 %n) {
+; ASM-LABEL: fp_frame:
+; ASM:         ldy __rc0
+; ASM-NEXT:    sty __rc30
+; ASM-NEXT:    ldy __rc1
+; ASM-NEXT:    sty __rc31
+; ASM-NEXT:    .cfi_escape 0x16, 0x80, 0x80, 0x0c, 0x05, 0x92, 0x8f, 0x80, 0x0c, 0x00
+; ASM:         jsr use
+; ASM-NEXT:    ldx __rc30
+; ASM-NEXT:    stx __rc0
+; ASM-NEXT:    ldx __rc31
+; ASM-NEXT:    stx __rc1
+; ASM-NEXT:    .cfi_escape 0x16, 0x80, 0x80, 0x0c, 0x05, 0x92, 0x80, 0x80, 0x0c, 0x00
+; ASM-NEXT:    pla
+; CFI:       FDE
+; CFI:         DW_CFA_val_expression: RS0 DW_OP_bregx RS15+0
+; CFI:         DW_CFA_val_expression: RS0 DW_OP_bregx RS0+0
+; CFI:         DW_CFA_restore_extended: RS0
+  %vla = alloca i8, i16 %n
+  call void @use(ptr %vla)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; An interrupt handler that calls out saves registers beyond the four that go
+; to the hardware stack on the soft stack, below a frame that also covers the
+; extra page subtracted for atomicity. The save slot rules must name the slots
+; the stores actually write.
+define void @isr() "interrupt" {
+; The interrupt-entry layout is described from the first instruction, before
+; the CLD: CFA = S+4, PC from S+2/S+3 (no +1), P at S+1.
+; ASM-LABEL: isr:
+; ASM:         .cfi_startproc
+; ASM-NEXT:  ; %bb.0:
+; ASM-NEXT:    .cfi_escape 0x0f, 0x09, 0x74, 0x04,
+; ASM-NEXT:    .cfi_escape 0x16, 0x05, 0x1a, 0x74, 0x02,
+; ASM-NEXT:    .cfi_escape 0x16, 0x04, 0x09, 0x74, 0x03,
+; ASM-NEXT:    .cfi_escape 0x10, 0x03, 0x09, 0x74, 0x01,
+; ASM-NEXT:    cld
+; The prologue subtracts 17 + 256 = 273 (adding 0xfeef).
+; ASM:         adc #239
+; ASM-NEXT:    sta __rc0
+; ASM-NEXT:    lda __rc1
+; ASM-NEXT:    adc #254
+; ASM-NEXT:    sta __rc1
+; ASM-NEXT:    .cfi_escape 0x16, 0x80, 0x80, 0x0c, 0x06, 0x92, 0x80, 0x80, 0x0c, 0x91, 0x02
+; The first soft-stack save writes RC3 to (RS0),16 and the last writes RC19 to
+; (RS0),0. The extra page is not part of these offsets.
+; ASM:         lda __rc3
+; ASM-NEXT:    ldy #16
+; ASM-NEXT:    sta (__rc0),y
+; ASM:         lda __rc19
+; ASM-NEXT:    dey
+; ASM-NEXT:    sta (__rc0),y
+; ASM:         rti
+; CFI:       FDE
+; CFI:         DW_CFA_val_expression: RS0 DW_OP_bregx RS0+273
+; CFI:         DW_CFA_expression: RC3 DW_OP_bregx RS0+16
+; CFI:         DW_CFA_expression: RC19 DW_OP_bregx RS0+0
+; CFI:         DW_CFA_restore_extended: RC3
+; CFI:         DW_CFA_restore_extended: RC19
+; CFI-NEXT:    DW_CFA_advance_loc:
+; CFI-NEXT:    DW_CFA_restore_extended: RS0
+  call void @ext()
+  ret void
+}
+
+; With more than one epilogue, a block laid out after the first one still runs
+; inside the frame; CFIFixup must restore the frame state for it. Tail merging
+; would otherwise merge the two epilogues into one.
+define i8 @two_epilogues(i8 %n) {
+; ASM-LABEL: two_epilogues:
+; ASM:         pha
+; ASM-NEXT:    .cfi_escape
+; ASM-NEXT:    .cfi_escape
+; ASM-NEXT:    .cfi_escape
+; ASM-NEXT:    .cfi_remember_state
+; ASM:         .cfi_restore llvm_mos_rs0
+; ASM:         rts
+; ASM-NEXT:  .LBB3_2:
+; ASM-NEXT:    .cfi_restore_state
+; In the row table: after the entry row, the first row back in the entry state
+; (CFA = S+3, RS0 = same) is the one after the first epilogue; the next block
+; is back inside the frame (CFA = S+4, RS0 = RS0+4).
+; CFI:       FDE
+; CFI:         DW_CFA_remember_state:
+; CFI:         DW_CFA_restore_state:
+; CFI:         CFA=DW_OP_breg4 S+3,{{.*}} RS0=same
+; CFI:         CFA=DW_OP_breg4 S+3,{{.*}} RS0=same
+; CFI-NEXT:    CFA=DW_OP_breg4 S+4,{{.*}} RS0=DW_OP_bregx RS0+4
+entry:
+  %buf = alloca [4 x i8]
+  call void @use(ptr %buf)
+  %r = call i8 @g(i8 %n)
+  %c = icmp eq i8 %r, 5
+  br i1 %c, label %a, label %b, !prof !0
+a:
+  ret i8 %r
+b:
+  %t = call i8 @g(i8 %r)
+  %u = add i8 %t, %n
+  ret i8 %u
+}
+
+!0 = !{!"branch_weights", i32 1000, i32 1}

+; With a frame pointer, RS0 moves in the body (here, to allocate the VLA). The
+; CFA stays hardware-stack based; instead, once the frame pointer (RS15) is set,
+; the caller's RS0 is described relative to it. The epilogue copies the frame
+; pointer back into RS0 before restoring the callee-saved registers, which may
+; include the frame pointer itself, so the rule moves back to RS0 there. The

+  ret void
